summary: Round 13, narrow re-check against the round-12 bytes (2d106c00). Still prose only: no production logic, no wire change, and nothing in this diff adds, moves or authorises an object-store request. I checked the two named edits and what they touch, did not re-derive a decision or a counted fact, and did not go looking for minors. BOTH EDITS HOLD, AND NEITHER BREAKS ANYTHING I PASSED AT ROUNDS 9-12. (A) My round-12 major is closed by DELETION, as prescribed: `grep -ci 'constant.in.k|constancy|kills every mutation'` over docs/, scripts/ and the root markdown returns hits only in backlog.md:69 and :126, and in both the word appears solely inside the 'AN EARLIER DRAFT SAID' retraction -- the flat equivalence claim is gone from the tree, not annotated, and no ADR, javadoc or research banner restates it (the half-landed-fix shape this row names three times). What survives carries the coverage the deleted sentence was supposed to carry, and carries it exactly: 'Naming the two invocations keeps the exactness the literal had: it reds 2, 64 and 128 alike, and still admits M5.66's header-plus-slice shape'. I re-walked the four mutations against the operative criterion 1 wording -- at most one fetchDirectory and at most one fetchRange invocation per (node, segment) -- and each lands where it must: per-run reports 64 fetchRange and reds; the (segmentKey, indexId) cache reports 2 fetchRange and reds, which is the indices-per-node scaling non-negotiable 6 forbids by name; the empty-array coalescer reds on the untouched decode half ('ALL K RUNS DECODE THEIR OWN RECORDS FROM IT'); M5.66's header-plus-slice greens at 1 and 1 with no edit to a landed assertion. The test role's second failure mode is closed by the same deletion: fetchCount(K=64) == fetchCount(K=2) is not a form the surviving text authorises, because the count is now named per invocation kind per (node, segment) rather than as a function of K. M5.66's resolution paragraph describes M5.45h in the same two named invocations, so the two cells still agree after the deletion and no cross-reference dangles. (B) M5.66's (iii) second-fixture clause now names its two Ks, and the arithmetic is this cell's own: AVG_RUN_BYTES 5,243 and crossover 169 give the proxy threshold 169*5,243 = 886,067; doubled runs at K = crossover give 169*10,486 = 1,772,134 > 886,067, so the sum(byteLen) proxy takes whole-object where the K-based path takes bounded and reds; halved runs at K = crossover + 1 give 170*2,621 = 445,570 <= 886,067, so the proxy takes bounded where the K-based path takes whole-object and reds. I checked the other ten of the twelve (K, run-size) choices and every one agrees -- doubled at K = 1, 2, 64 and at 170 and ~400, halved at K = 1, 2, 64, 169 and ~400 -- so 'the only two that red' is exact and the earlier shape-without-a-K wording was indeed vacuous ten times in twelve. Both named cases are at a K already in the sampled evidence set, so the clause's own 'SAME K, different run sizes' requirement is met rather than quietly replaced by another K, and the structural reason given is sound: a proxy monotone in K that agrees at K = 1 must switch at some K' != crossover, and the disagreement band [min(K',crossover)+1, max(K',crossover)] always terminates at the crossover, which is why the falsifying case is always at the boundary and why an interior sample such as K = 64 cannot be relied on (under doubled runs the proxy switches at K = 84, above 64). (C) Nothing else moved. The edits touch no other clause: the two-sided boundary pair, invariants (i)/(ii)/(iii), the K = 1 and K = 2 extremes fixture, the K = 64 below-the-switch case, the symmetric round-trip predicate, the codec read-and-refuse arm, 3b's extent disagreement, the count-every-request-at-the-seam clause, the withdrawn cross-AZ arm, security.md rule 3's handoff, and the M5.45g + M5.45h + M5.62 dependency chain are all unchanged and each still reds its named mutation. On the axis that matters here, both edits move request-rate enforcement tighter, not looser: (A) removes the only sentence that licensed a count form under which an indices-per-node cache passes, and (B) removes the only reading of (iii) under which a path switching on extents rather than on K passes at every asserted share. NOTHING REMAINS THAT WOULD CHANGE A DECISION OR LET A WRONG IMPLEMENTATION PASS.
